To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the dynamic nature of the ISMR–ENSO and ISMR–EQUINOO relationship can be captured using BDLM and (b) the concurrent effect of both ENSO and Equatorial Indian Oscillation (EIO) on monthly variation of rainfall can be captured using the BDLM.
the Bayesian dynamic model captures the dynamic relationship of large-scale circulation with monthly ISMR and the model is able to predict monthly rainfall with a good degree of accuracy.

(1) the proposed model is able to capture the dynamic nature of the relationship between large-scale climatic variables and monthly rainfall, (2) the proposed model can predict the monthly rainfall in a better way than the conventional statistical models, and (3) the proposed model predicts the monthly rainfall in those years when ENSO is not able to predict ISMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (i) to develop a Bayesian dynamic model to predict the monthly rainfall in the Indian subcontinent, (ii) to investigate the effect of EQUINOO on monthly ISMR, (iii) to establish the concurrent effect of ENSO with EQUINOO in predicting the monthly ISMR, and (iv) to compare the efficacy of the proposed Bayesian dynamic model with a conventional regression model.
the prediction of Indian monthly rainfall, using Bayesian dynamic modeling and large-scale climatic indices.
the development of a robust model that is capable of predicting ISMR in a better way and also to identify the causal climatic variables, influencing ISMR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EQUINOO and ENSO are the two important large-scale circulation indices influencing the monthly ISMR and their concurrent effect should be considered for a robust and reliable prediction of ISMR in a dynamic manner.
ENSO and Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) have a significant impact on Indian monsoon rainfall.
the monthly variation of ISM rainfall is influenced by the simultaneous effect of ENSO, EQUINOO and other climatic variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EQUINOO has been established as an additional factor influencing the Indian monthly rainfall, and it can be considered as an important variable along with ENSOs for the prediction of monthly ISMR.
the proposed Bayesian approach is a better way to model the dynamic behavior of ISMR and its relationship with ENSO and Equatorial Indian ocean oscillation (EQUINoo).

the proposed model (BDLM), with EQUINOO information, is able to model the Indian monthly rainfall in a better way than ENSO information alone, especially in those years (1997, 1999, 2002) when the correlation between ENSOs and ISMR is negative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic relationship between ENSO, EQUINOO and ISMR is better captured by BDLM.
EQUINOO has an important role in the dynamics of ISMR, and its concurrent effect along with that of ENSO should be considered in the prediction of ISMR.
BDLM can be used as a tool for predicting the monthly variation of ISM rainfall.
